description: Create, update and delete an Azure Container Instance.

parameters.name: acr_identity
parameters.description: The Identity to use for access to the registry server.

parameters.name: ad_user
parameters.description: Active Directory username. Use when authenticating with an Active Directory user rather than service principal.

parameters.name: adfs_authority_url
parameters.description: Azure AD authority url. Use when authenticating with Username/password, and has your own ADFS authority.

parameters.name: api_profile
parameters.description: Selects an API profile to use when communicating with Azure services. Default value of latest is appropriate for public clouds; future values will allow use with Azure Stack. Default: "latest"

parameters.name: append_tags
parameters.description: Use to control if tags field is canonical or just appends to existing tags. When canonical, any tags not found in the tags parameter will be removed from the object’s metadata. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: auth_source
parameters.description: Controls the source of the credentials to use for authentication. Can also be set via the ANSIBLE_AZURE_AUTH_SOURCE environment variable. When set to auto (the default) the precedence is module parameters -> env -> credential_file -> cli. When set to env, the credentials will be read from the environment variables When set to credential_file, it will read the profile from ~/.azure/credentials. When set to cli, the credentials will be sources from the Azure CLI profile. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if more than one is present otherwise the default az cli subscription is used. When set to msi, the host machine must be an azure resource with an enabled MSI extension. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if the resource is granted access to more than one subscription, otherwise the first subscription is chosen. The msi was added in Ansible 2.6. Choices: "auto" ← (default) "cli" "credential_file" "env" "msi"

parameters.name: cert_validation_mode
parameters.description: Controls the certificate validation behavior for Azure endpoints. By default, all modules will validate the server certificate, but when an HTTPS proxy is in use, or against Azure Stack, it may be necessary to disable this behavior by passing ignore. Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CERT_VALIDATION environment variable. Choices: "ignore" "validate"

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Azure client ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal or Managed Identity (msi). Can also be set via the AZURE_CLIENT_ID environment variable.

parameters.name: cloud_environment
parameters.description: For cloud environments other than the US public cloud, the environment name (as defined by Azure Python SDK, eg, AzureChinaCloud, AzureUSGovernment), or a metadata discovery endpoint URL (required for Azure Stack). Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CLOUD_ENVIRONMENT environment variable. Default: "AzureCloud"

parameters.name: containers
parameters.description: List of containers. Required when creation.

parameters.name: commands
parameters.description: List of commands to execute within the container instance in exec form. When updating existing container all existing commands will be replaced by new ones.

parameters.name: cpu
parameters.description: The required number of CPU cores of the containers. Default: 1.0

parameters.name: environment_variables
parameters.description: List of container environment variables. When updating existing container all existing variables will be replaced by new ones.

parameters.name: is_secure
parameters.description: Is variable secure. Choices: false true

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Environment variable name.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Environment variable value.

parameters.name: image
parameters.description: The container image name.

parameters.name: memory
parameters.description: The required memory of the containers in GB. Default: 1.5

parameters.name: ports
parameters.description: List of ports exposed within the container group.

parameters.name: volume_mounts
parameters.description: The volume mounts for the container instance

parameters.name: mount_path
parameters.description: The path within the container where the volume should be mounted

parameters.name: read_only
parameters.description: The flag indicating whether the volume mount is read-only Choices: false true

parameters.name: disable_instance_discovery
parameters.description: Determines whether or not instance discovery is performed when attempting to authenticate. Setting this to true will completely disable both instance discovery and authority validation. This functionality is intended for use in scenarios where the metadata endpoint cannot be reached such as in private clouds or Azure Stack. The process of instance discovery entails retrieving authority metadata from https://login.microsoft.com/ to validate the authority. By setting this to **True**, the validation of the authority is disabled. As a result, it is crucial to ensure that the configured authority host is valid and trustworthy. Set via credential file profile or the AZURE_DISABLE_INSTANCE_DISCOVERY environment variable. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: dns_name_label
parameters.description: The Dns name label for the IP.

parameters.name: force_update
parameters.description: Force update of existing container instance. Any update will result in deletion and recreation of existing containers. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: identity
parameters.description: Identity for the Server.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the managed identity Choices: "SystemAssigned" "SystemAssigned, UserAssigned" "UserAssigned" Default: "None"

parameters.name: user_assigned_identities
parameters.description: User Assigned Managed Identities and its options Default: {}

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: List of the user assigned identities IDs associated to the VM Default: []

parameters.name: ip_address
parameters.description: The IP address type of the container group. Default is none and creating an instance without public IP. Choices: "public" "none" ← (default) "private"

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Valid azure location. Defaults to location of the resource group.

parameters.name: log_mode
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: log_path
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: os_type
parameters.description: The OS type of containers. Choices: "linux" ← (default) "windows" "Linux" "Windows"

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Active Directory user password. Use when authenticating with an Active Directory user rather than service principal.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Security profile found in ~/.azure/credentials file.

parameters.name: registry_login_server
parameters.description: The container image registry login server.

parameters.name: registry_password
parameters.description: The password to log in container image registry server.

parameters.name: registry_username
parameters.description: The username to log in container image registry server.

parameters.name: resource_group
parameters.description: Name of resource group.

parameters.name: restart_policy
parameters.description: Restart policy for all containers within the container group. Choices: "always" "on_failure" "never"

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: Azure client secret. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Assert the state of the container instance. Use present to create or update an container instance and absent to delete it. Choices: "absent" "present" ← (default)

parameters.name: subnet_ids
parameters.description: The subnet resource IDs for a container group. Multiple subnets are not yet supported. Only 1 subnet can be used.

parameters.name: subscription_id
parameters.description: Your Azure subscription Id.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Dictionary of string:string pairs to assign as metadata to the object. Metadata tags on the object will be updated with any provided values. To remove tags set append_tags option to false. Currently, Azure DNS zones and Traffic Manager services also don’t allow the use of spaces in the tag. Azure Front Door doesn’t support the use of Azure Automation and Azure CDN only support 15 tags on resources.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: Azure tenant ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: thumbprint
parameters.description: The thumbprint of the private key specified in x509_certificate_path. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal. Required if x509_certificate_path is defined.

parameters.name: volumes
parameters.description: List of Volumes that can be mounted by containers in this container group.

parameters.name: azure_file
parameters.description: The Azure File volume

parameters.name: share_name
parameters.description: The name of the Azure File share to be mounted as a volume

parameters.name: storage_account_key
parameters.description: The storage account access key used to access the Azure File share

parameters.name: storage_account_name
parameters.description: The name of the storage account that contains the Azure File share

parameters.name: empty_dir
parameters.description: The empty directory volume

parameters.name: git_repo
parameters.description: The git repo volume

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: Target directory name

parameters.name: repository
parameters.description: Repository URL

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Commit hash for the specified revision

parameters.name: x509_certificate_path
parameters.description: Path to the X509 certificate used to create the service principal in PEM format. The certificate must be appended to the private key. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

examples:
- name: Create sample container group
  azure_rm_containerinstance:
    resource_group: myResourceGroup
    name: myContainerInstanceGroup
    os_type: linux
    ip_address: public
    containers:
      - name: myContainer1
        image: httpd
        memory: 1.5
        ports:
          - 80
          - 81

- name: Create sample container group with azure file share volume
  azure_rm_containerinstance:
    resource_group: myResourceGroup
    name: myContainerInstanceGroupz
    os_type: linux
    ip_address: public
    containers:
      - name: mycontainer1
        image: httpd
        memory: 1
        volume_mounts:
          - name: filesharevolume
            mount_path: "/data/files"
        ports:
          - 80
          - 81
    volumes:
      - name: filesharevolume
        azure_file:
          storage_account_name: mystorageaccount
          share_name: acishare
          storage_account_key: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

- name: Create sample container group with git repo volume
  azure_rm_containerinstance:
    resource_group: myResourceGroup
    name: myContainerInstanceGroup
    os_type: linux
    ip_address: public
    containers:
      - name: mycontainer1
        image: httpd
        memory: 1
        volume_mounts:
          - name: myvolume1
            mount_path: "/mnt/test"
        ports:
          - 80
          - 81
    volumes:
      - name: myvolume1
        git_repo:
          repository: "https://github.com/Azure-Samples/aci-helloworld.git"

- name: Create sample container instance with subnet
  azure_rm_containerinstance:
    resource_group: myResourceGroup
    name: myContainerInstanceGroup
    os_type: linux
    ip_address: private
    location: eastus
    subnet_ids:
      - "{{ subnet_id }}"
    ports:
      - 80
    containers:
      - name: mycontainer1
        image: httpd
        memory: 1.5
        ports:
          - 80
          - 81

return_values.name: containers
return_values.description: The containers within the container group. Returned: always Sample: [{"commands": null, "cpu": 1.0, "environment_variables": null, "image": "httpd", "memory": 1.0, "name": "mycontainer1", "ports": [80, 81], "volume_mounts": [{"mount_path": "/data/files", "name": "filesharevolume", "read_only": false}]}]

return_values.name: ip_address
return_values.description: Public IP Address of created container group. Returned: if address is public Sample: "175.12.233.11"

return_values.name: provisioning_state
return_values.description: Provisioning state of the container. Returned: always Sample: "Creating"

return_values.name: volumes
return_values.description: The list of volumes that mounted by containers in container group Returned: if volumes specified

return_values.name: azure_file
return_values.description: Azure file share volume details Returned: If Azure file share type of volume requested Sample: {"read_only": null, "share_name": "acishare", "storage_account_key": "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", "storage_account_name": "mystorageaccount"}

return_values.name: empty_dir
return_values.description: Empty directory volume details Returned: If Empty directory type of volume requested Sample: {}

return_values.name: git_repo
return_values.description: Git Repo volume details Returned: If Git repo type of volume requested Sample: {"directory": null, "repository": "https://github.com/Azure-Samples/aci-helloworld.git", "revision": null}

return_values.name: name
return_values.description: The name of the Volume Returned: always Sample: "filesharevolume"

return_values.name: secret
return_values.description: Secret volume details Returned: If Secret type of volume requested Sample: {}
